mentl/d1c45fa:
$field_byte_offset (seed lower) resolved the field name via list_index(entry, 0),
but TRecord field entries are field_pair RECORDS ($field_pair_make, FIELD_PAIR=203),
not tuples — list_index reads a record as a flat list and yields the wrong slot,
so the name came back "". str_eq never matched -> every multi-field `.field`
collapsed to offset 0 (the first field). Since $resolve_field_offset runs at
seed-compile-time to resolve the WHEEL's field accesses, the seed emitted offset 0
for every `.field` in the wheel -> mentl2 read field 0 everywhere. `placement.slot`
(3rd field) thus read `ename` (a string pointer) -> grow_to_with_gaps(_, huge) ->
out-of-bounds. That was the post-fold pass-2 blocker.

Fix: read the name via $field_pair_name (record_get offset 0), consistent with how
$infer_walk_expr_make_record builds the entries and how the sibling readers
($resolve_from_record_open merge at 1394-95, etc.) already read them. Removed a
leftover debug eprint in $resolve_field_offset_from_ty while here.

The wheel does this correctly (TRecord fields are tuples, read by tuple-destructure)
so mentl3 matches; the seed's field_pair representation computes the SAME offset
(sorted-index*4), so byte-parity holds.

mentl/d1714f5:
Diagnosis checkpoint for the indirect-call-type-mismatch that traps mentl2
on its own machinery (even on `fn main(x)=x`) and collapses pass3 to 0 funcs.

Root: a perform of a handler-dispatched op with no lexical handler in scope
was statically bound to a global default-handler-per-op map (the
$lower_resolve_handler_for_op fallback). The shared iterate_from's
`perform yield` thus called op_map_collector_yield for every collector, so
for_each/fold/filter misbound to map_collector's state -> wrong offset ->
garbage funcref -> trap.

Step 1 (this commit): delete the default-handler fallback so a no-lexical-
handler resolution returns 0 -> LEvPerform (evidence dispatch). A perform
reads the handler stack at the perform site; it never guesses a global
default (protocol_reflexive_interiority: the observer is interior).

This exposes the true L1 gate: the seed's evidence-passing is stubbed
(derive_ev_slots returns the empty list; the iterate call lowers as LCall,
not LSuspend), and "one record, four roles" (handler IS state IS closure IS
evidence) has four un-coordinated offset conventions plus no record
threading. The coordinated build -- derive_ev_slots + LSuspend threading +
LEvPerform load + fence-relative offsets + LStateSlotStore unification,
seed and wheel in lockstep -- is the next arc.

Walkthrough docs/specs/simulations/Hbeta-perform-evidence-dispatch.md
records the full diagnosis and the unified-record-layout resolution (sec 4.5).
mentl2 still traps (L1 was blocked either way; no green regression).
mentl/d1aade1:
Replaced nested if/else + str_eq(op, '+') == 1 chains with
clean match dispatch:
  classify_binop(op): match op → 'arithmetic'/'comparison'/etc
  infer_binop: match classify_binop(op) → typed constraints
  infer_unaryop: match op { 'Neg' => ..., 'Not' => ... }

This is what Inka looks like at its best: no str_eq calls,
no nested if/else, pure structural dispatch.
